terms.gloss: take out; take or scoop out
terms.comment: “Core” and “deseed” are expressed with ordinary objects and verbs rather than unsupported one-word technical coinages. Ordinary Latin verbs cover the actions: scooping is expressed with eximere plus the spoon as an instrument; no separate unsupported kitchen neologism is required.

evidence: Apic. 4.2.15: ā superficiē versās in discum
terms.comment: Apicius’s phrase for turning a set dish over onto a plate; his patina versātilis is a dish made to be turned out (Apic. 4.2.2, 4.2.16).

phrases.english: Scoop out the avocado flesh with a spoon.

phrases.latin: Placenta cocta est; ē furnō exime.
phrases.english: The cake is done; take it out of the oven.

phrases.latin: Ubi cocta erit, eximitō et melle unguitō.
phrases.english: When it is baked, take it out and spread it with honey.

phrases.latin: Fōrmam in discum versā; placenta facile exībit.
phrases.english: Turn the tin over onto a plate; the cake will come out easily.

phrases.latin: Ā superficiē versās in discum, piper aspergēs
phrases.english: Turn it out onto a dish, top side down, and sprinkle it with pepper

phrases.latin: deinde ut fōrmīs aut calathīs exēmptus est
